column1: # Purpose: Gold labels for English story passages (original text, written for this set; free to use).
# Format: one sentence per line: text<TAB>speaker<TAB>feeling. Speaker "-" is narration only (no speech).
# A blank line ends a paragraph. "@ id" starts a passage, "@cast Name=F|M ..." lists its characters.
# Feelings: neutral joy sad angry scared surprised soft loud. A quoted line's feeling is how the words are said.
Mira came home late, her shoes in her hand.
He had waited up for two hours.
“The last train broke down outside Rugby.”
He looked at her for a long moment, and then his face softened.
Grace opened the envelope with shaking fingers.
Inside was a single sheet, folded twice.
“What does it say?” asked Mr Hale.
She read it twice before she could answer.
“After all these years, they found him.”
She laughed and cried at once, and the letter fell to the floor.
The market was loud with traders calling out their prices.
Ravi stopped at a stall heaped with mangoes.
“Two hundred,” said the old woman behind the counter.
“Fair enough,” he said, and counted out the notes.
Waves broke over the rail and the deck tipped under their feet.
“Get that sail down before it takes the mast!”
Jonah clung to a rope, too frightened to move.
Lily found her grandmother in the garden, kneeling among the roses.
‘Did you plant all of these?’ she asked.
‘Your grandfather gave me the first one the year we married.’
The old woman was quiet for a while.
‘Every single day,’ she said at last.
Inspector Ward set his notebook on the table.
“Mrs Patel, where were you on Tuesday night?”
The twins burst into the kitchen together.
“First prize,” Arjun added, holding up the cup.
Their mother put down her spoon.
“Then I suppose,” said their mother, smiling, “we're having cake tonight.”
Something moved in the dark at the end of the corridor.
“It's only the house settling,” she murmured.
